transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is, I’ve been kind of stuck on how my face looks lately. We had this brighter mirror put in the bathroom, and ever since then I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and my jaw, like it looks uneven or saggy to me.

My husband keeps saying he doesn’t really see what I’m talking about, but I do. And it’s silly because it’s just a mirror, but you know how bathroom lighting can make everything look worse? We only changed it because the old one was terrible for putting on makeup, and now I almost wish we hadn’t.
Have you found yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking the mirror, touching your face, or comparing your appearance to others, because of your concerns about your face?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t stand there for hours or anything, but most mornings I do end up checking my face from a few different angles before I leave. Especially if I have to go to the courthouse, because the lighting there is so harsh too—those fluorescent lights make everybody look tired, honestly.

I’ll usually put on a little extra makeup if I feel like my cheeks or jaw look off. And I do catch myself comparing my face to other women at work sometimes, like wondering if their skin looks firmer or if I look older next to them. I hate admitting that. I’ve also avoided being in casual pictures if I’m not feeling okay about how I look that day.
Do these concerns about your face ever cause you a lot of distress or get in the way of things you need or want to do, like going out, taking pictures, or even going to work?

Yeah… I mean, I still do what I have to do. I’m not missing work or anything like that. But it does kind of interfere in little ways.

Like, I’ll spend too long getting ready, trying to fix my makeup or checking if my face looks strange, and then I’m rushing into the courthouse right at the last minute. A couple mornings I’ve cut it really close. And I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once because I couldn’t just leave the house when I meant to.

And with pictures… I’ve skipped a few casual photos, like at book club or community things. Which is ridiculous, because it’s not like anyone’s framing them in a museum, you know? But I just don’t want to see my face later and feel awful about it.
Do you feel that your concerns about your face are something that others would notice, or do you think they might not see what you’re seeing?

I think… I think other people probably don’t see it the way I do. My husband says he can’t really tell what I’m talking about, which almost makes me feel more ridiculous, but when I look in that brighter bathroom mirror, the skin around my cheeks and jaw just looks uneven or kind of saggy to me.

And I know mirrors can be weird—like dressing room mirrors are the worst, don’t even get me started—but it still feels very obvious when I’m the one looking at it.

Would you say that the way your face looks—specifically the skin around your cheeks and jaw—is something that you believe is noticeably off or unattractive, even though others may not really see it the way you do?

Yes… that’s pretty much it. Since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw, like it looks uneven or a little saggy to me. My husband says he doesn’t really see what I’m talking about, and he’s usually pretty honest—sometimes too honest, honestly, like when I ask if leftovers are still good and he gives me this whole lecture about dates on containers.

But with my face, I don’t know… I can see it. Even if other people don’t. It just looks off to me.
Have you noticed any changes in your skin or facial muscles that might explain the unevenness or sagging you see, like numbness, tingling, or weakness on one side of your face?

I don’t think so… I mean, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I don’t really know what facial muscle weakness would feel like, exactly, but I haven’t had some obvious thing where one side stops moving or anything.

It’s more just when I’m looking in the mirror, especially that bathroom one. And then I start leaning closer, turning my face different ways, which probably makes it worse. My husband says the lighting in there is too harsh—he wanted one of those softer bulbs, but then I said I need to actually see what I’m doing, and somehow that became a whole Saturday errand.

But no, I haven’t noticed numbness or tingling or… anything like that.
Do you believe that the way your face looks—specifically the skin around your cheeks and jaw—is noticeably flawed or unattractive, even when others don’t seem to notice it?

Yes… I do. I mean, I know my husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about, and maybe other people aren’t looking that closely, but since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep seeing it.

It’s mostly around my cheeks and jaw, like the skin looks uneven or kind of saggy to me. And then I get stuck on it. It’s silly because I’ll be trying to get ready for work, and I’m supposed to be thinking about filings or whatever’s due that day, and instead I’m standing there turning my face in the light like that’s going to solve anything.

But yes… to me it looks noticeably off, even if other people don’t notice it.
Would you say that the way your cheeks and jaw look is something that others would not even notice, but it feels very obvious to you?

Yes… that’s exactly how it feels. Like, I know my husband says he can’t really see it, and maybe if someone passed me in the grocery store they wouldn’t think anything. But to me, in that brighter bathroom mirror, the skin around my cheeks and jaw just looks uneven, kind of saggy.

And then I start wondering how I didn’t notice it before—though that mirror is honestly too bright, my husband said that from the beginning, and I told him if we’re going to replace a mirror we might as well get one where I can actually see what I’m doing. But now I see too much, I guess.

So yes… other people might not notice it, but to me it’s very obvious.
Do you often feel anxious or preoccupied with the idea that your face might look flawed, even when you can’t clearly see the problem or when others don’t notice it?

Yes… I do get anxious about it. It’s like once I think about it, I can’t really leave it alone.

I’m here because ever since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or kind of saggy to me. My husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about, which should probably make me feel better, but it doesn’t always. I’ll still be thinking, “Well, maybe he’s just being nice,” or “Maybe it only shows in certain light.”

And then I’m late getting ready because I’m staring at it, and I’m supposed to be getting to work—there’s always some file or deadline—and instead I’m in the bathroom turning my face different ways. So yes, even if I can’t point to it clearly or other people don’t notice, it still feels like something’s wrong.
